terms.comment: Our name for the airport: Traupman’s āëroportus (p. 215) with Bergomās, Bergomātis, the adjective of Bergomum, which Lewis & Short has from inscriptions, where it is said of the town as a mūnicipium and a rēs pūblica; the townspeople are Bergomātēs (Plin. NH 3.125, Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens gives the same adjective (s.v. Bergamo). The genitive is āëroportūs Bergomātis. No reference work has a name for the airport.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 215.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Bergamo.
